posts.title: Catch up after a week away from the Sheet
posts.description: SMS kept arriving while you were away. Sort that week by amount in your Google Sheet, fix the large rows, drop duplicates, add cash you remember, and stop.

posts.title: Train, flight, and hotel: what one trip actually cost
posts.description: The ticket is not the trip. Tag the train or flight, hotel, cabs, and meals with one trip name in your Google Sheet and sum that filter when you get home.

posts.title: Annual insurance premium month: health and vehicle
posts.description: A yearly health or vehicle premium is one large debit, not a weekly leak. Log it on the day it leaves, and use a monthly set-aside so your Google Sheet is not surprised.

posts.title: Refunds and reversals: do not leave a returned spend as a loss
posts.description: A refund or a failed UPI is not new income. Match the credit to the original debit in your Google Sheet so a cancelled spend does not stay on the books as a loss.

posts.title: ATM cash and the notes that vanish without an SMS
posts.description: An ATM withdrawal moves money into your pocket. Log the cash spends or the withdrawal, not both, so the month in your Google Sheet is not doubled.

posts.title: Flatmate splits: electricity, wifi, and the maid
posts.description: One flatmate often pays the bill and collects shares. Log the bill once in your Google Sheet and the repayments as transfers so the home cost is not tripled.

posts.title: 1 October: close September and start the new month in the Sheet
posts.description: On the 1st, finish September's blank categories, write three totals, and set October caps only after rent, EMIs, and savings are listed in the same Google Sheet.

posts.title: Client UPI on the same phone as household spend
posts.description: Freelance payments, software bills, and the kirana share one phone. Label business in and business out in your Google Sheet so a client credit is not treated as spendable pay.

posts.title: Money sent to parents each month: how to record it
posts.description: A monthly transfer home is a real outflow. Give it a family category in your Google Sheet so extras do not hide inside misc or become the new regular amount.

posts.title: Weekend food delivery: the Swiggy and Zomato leak
posts.description: Friday to Sunday orders look like single treats. Add fees and tips in your Google Sheet, set a cap on Friday, and check it before a third order.

posts.title: SIP and RD are not the same as spending
posts.description: A SIP or RD debit leaves your account, but it is not wasted spend. Label it as savings in your Google Sheet so groceries are not blamed for money you moved on purpose.

posts.title: Rent paid by UPI: what to store so you can show it later
posts.description: A rent UPI needs the month, the landlord, and the reference already in the SMS. Keep that in your Google Sheet so you can show the payment without a gallery of screenshots.

posts.title: Pharmacy and lab bills: keep them out of groceries
posts.description: Medicine, lab tests, and chemist cash are health costs. File them in your Google Sheet apart from groceries so a medical month does not look like a food leak.

posts.title: Petrol and FASTag: track the real commute cost
posts.description: Pump payments and FASTag tolls are both the cost of getting to work. Add them in one Google Sheet, separate from weekend trips, without counting a tag recharge twice.

posts.title: School fees, books and bus: term payments in the Sheet
posts.description: Term fees, bus, books and annual charges hit in a cluster. Split them in your Google Sheet so a fee month is a plan, not a shock you blame on groceries.

posts.title: Credit card swipe and the later bill: do not double count
posts.description: The card swipe is the spend. The UPI you send later to pay the card bill is a settlement. Log them differently in your Google Sheet so the month is not doubled.

posts.title: Kirana cash plus UPI: keep one grocery ledger
posts.description: The neighbourhood shop often takes notes for loose items and UPI for the rest. Log both in the same Google Sheet so the monthly grocery number is real.
